back: Frequency density $\times$ class width (the area of the bar).
A diagram for grouped continuous data with touching bars, in which the area of each bar represents the frequency.

front: What must the bar heights be when class widths are unequal?
Do histogram bars have gaps between them?
back: No: the data are continuous, so the bars touch.

front: How do you estimate how many values lie in part of a class?
back: Assume the values are spread evenly: take the same fraction of the frequency as the fraction of the class width.
A graph joining the points (class midpoint, frequency) with straight lines.

front: How is a frequency polygon closed? (ZIMSEC)
back: Join to the horizontal axis at the midpoints of the empty classes on each side.

front: Does the tallest bar of a histogram always have the largest frequency?
back: No: with unequal widths the tallest bar has the largest frequency density.

front: How do you find the scale of a histogram with no labelled density axis?
back: Use a complete class: frequency ÷ width gives the density shown by that bar's height.
